A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same combinatorial Gaussian-process bandit work despite the changed title and substantially revised experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit experiments on a synthetic network and SUMO simulations of Luxembourg and Monaco, including algorithm, kernel, and prior comparisons in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments using GP-generated energy costs on Luxembourg and Monaco road networks, including algorithm comparisons and sensitivity studies in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core selection rules, composite graph-feature kernel, and rectified routing procedure remain; Bayes-GP-UCB is renamed GP-BUCB. However, v2 Algorithm 3 removes v1's explicit Adam updates of kernel and likelihood parameters, while Appendix B.3 still specifies an Adam learning rate. It is unclear whether the optimization procedure changed or its description became incomplete.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates a synthetic grid and traffic simulations on Luxembourg and Monaco. v2 removes the grid and replaces the traffic environments with GP-generated energy costs on the retained road topologies. Monaco coverage also changes from one evaluation route to two. These changes substantially alter the represented navigation scenarios.

E2.justification: v1's principal algorithm comparison evaluates GP and Bayesian-inference models with BUCB and Thompson sampling. v2 retains these combinations and adds GP-UCB and BI-UCB to the actual comparison in Figure 2. This is a limited expansion of the comparator set; the BUCB name change is not a new method.

E3.justification: The city-network horizon changes from 200 to 500 rounds, and reported random regret based on an estimated best route is replaced by cumulative regret under generated rewards. The prior and reward-generation settings change substantially. The stated GP optimization budget changes from batches of 8000 with five gradient steps to batches of 2500 with one step; v2 also introduces confidence-parameter and lengthscale sweep protocols.

E4.justification: v1's comparisons of five kernel compositions and three levels of prior informativeness disappear. v2 instead tests UCB/BUCB confidence parametrizations and kernel lengthscales from 0.1 to 2.0, with extended results in Appendix C.1. Exploration visualizations are also replaced with comparisons covering all six algorithms on four routes, changing the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v1 specifies ten repetitions for synthetic-network experiments and five for city-network experiments. v2 specifies five repetitions per configuration throughout its replacement experimental suite. Means and standard errors remain the reporting practice; the removed ten-run experiments do not establish a reduction in repetitions for a matched experiment.

E6.justification: The earlier synthetic results, city energy-consumption table, and visited-edge counts are removed. v2 reports replacement 500-round results, including GP-BUCB versus GP-UCB and new parameter-sensitivity findings in Figures 2–6. These are not same-setting performance improvements. The new lengthscale plots generally show decreasing GP regret as lengthscale grows, although the accompanying sentence on page 10 incorrectly states an increase.

T1.justification: The regret bounds replace v1's noise-only constant with a factor involving the largest within-superarm posterior covariance eigenvalue. New Lemma A.12 supplies the corresponding variance/information-gain argument, changing the worst-case dependence on superarm size. Lemma 3.1 also adds the logarithmic case where ξ/ω equals one, while the main BUCB theorems specialize to ξ > ω > 1. These are substantive revisions beyond reorganizing existing proofs.

C1.justification: v1's introductory claim of sublinear dependence on superarm size is withdrawn; v2 acknowledges worst-case linear dependence in Section 3.1. The abstract drops the claim of reduced dependence on prior informativeness. Conversely, the introduction adds a claim that BUCB permits less exploration while retaining theoretical guarantees and broadens the novelty wording from the first Bayesian regret bound to the first regret bound for GP-BUCB.

C2.justification: v1's substantive discussion of inducing-point instability, optimization resets, clustering, graph-kernel assumptions, and prior-dependent behavior is removed. v2 adds interpretations of confidence-parameter tuning and theoretical qualifications concerning worst-case eigenvalue dependence and possible logarithmic improvements. The limitations of the retained inducing-point heuristic are no longer discussed.

D1.justification: Experimental documentation is substantially replaced: detailed SUMO initialization, synthetic-network construction, and prior-specific instructions disappear, while GP reward-generation parameters, GPyTorch implementation information, and exact route endpoint identifiers are supplied. The earlier disclosure of a 500-eigenpair graph-kernel approximation is absent. Kernel formulas and vehicle parameters are largely retained in Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: New Table 1 systematically positions the work against related GP-bandit theory. Section 3.1 changes the comparison with Nika et al. from v1's claimed advantage in superarm-size dependence to matching its order, and adds comparison with Takeno et al. (2024). References supporting offline navigation and discrete inducing-point discussions are removed, while newer theoretical and implementation references are added.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. Finite-case theory is brought into the main analysis, the separate application and experimental sections are consolidated, and kernel details move to Appendix B. The notation appendix and extended discussion disappear, while a dedicated experimental-results appendix is introduced. This substantially changes the document's organization and emphasis.

P2.justification: v2 adds the related-work comparison table and replaces the earlier experimental displays with compact multi-panel algorithm and sensitivity plots. Numerical result tables and the notation table disappear; exploration maps are redrawn and placed in Appendix C. Separate TS and BUCB pseudocode displays are combined with UCB, while the unchanged vehicle-parameter table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the central analysis by addressing the missing covariance dependence in v1's variance bound and qualifying the superarm-size claim; the added UCB and tuning comparisons are also useful. However, replacing traffic simulations with GP-generated costs and removing kernel/prior studies and substantive limitations weakens application and robustness support. The contradictory lengthscale summary adds a reporting defect. These substantial gains and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
